title: Nvidia dominates AI chips, but BofA sees AMD closing in

content_html:
Twenty years ago, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) spent the better part of a decade selling processors into a market Intel dominated, waiting for the moment Intel could not keep pace with demand on its own.

That moment eventually arrived, and AMD converted patience into real share of the server chip market. Bank of America now believes AI accelerators are heading toward a similar inflection, only compressed into a shorter window.

The bank reiterated its Buy rating on AMD on Aug. 4 and raised its long-term earnings estimates, arguing the company's real growth story has barely started.

AMD holds a low single-digit share of the AI accelerator market that Nvidia dominates, but BofA's whole thesis rests on that gap closing faster than the stock currently reflects.

According to a BofA Global Research note, AMD's earnings power could exceed $30 a share by 2030, roughly four times the $7.62 the bank expects for this year. That gap is the entire thesis.

BofA is telling investors to stop grading AMD on the next ninety days and start pricing in a business that looks nothing like today's by the end of the decade.

The bank's $620 price objective is built on 27 times its 2028 earnings estimate, in line with AMD's own five-year historical trading range.

Investors are still grading the next 90 days

The market has not caught up to that framing yet. AMD reported record second-quarter revenue of $11.5 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.66 a share, both ahead of Wall Street estimates, yet the stock fell as much as 9% the next session, according to CNBC.

Data center revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, but investors focused on flat margin guidance and rising capital spending tied to new AI infrastructure.

That reaction is exactly the kind of near-term noise BofA is telling clients to ignore. The bank's note argues that AMD's flagship rack-scale AI system, called Helios, will not meaningfully affect results until the fourth quarter, so judging the stock on this quarter's margin line misses the point entirely.

AMD is selling racks now, not just chips

Helios represents a shift in what AMD actually sells. Instead of shipping individual processors and graphics chips the way it has for decades, AMD is now packaging GPUs, CPUs, and networking hardware into complete rack systems, a format Nvidia has used for years to sell entire AI computers rather than loose components.

AMD has signed customers willing to bet on that shift at scale. Meta committed to as much as 6 gigawatts of AMD GPU capacity in a multi-year deal, and OpenAI struck a similar 6-gigawatt agreement, with Microsoft and Oracle also lined up to deploy Helios systems this year.

content_html_zh:
二十年前，Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) 花了十年的大部分时间向英特尔主导的市场销售处理器，等待英特尔无法独自跟上需求的那一刻。

那一刻最终到来了，AMD 将耐心转化为服务器芯片市场的真正份额。 美国银行现在认为人工智能加速器正在走向类似的转变，只是压缩到更短的窗口。

该银行于 8 月 4 日重申了对 AMD 的买入评级，并上调了长期盈利预期，认为该公司真正的增长故事才刚刚开始。

AMD 在 Nvidia 主导的人工智能加速器市场中占有较低的个位数份额，但美国银行的整个论点都基于这一差距的缩小速度快于该股目前反映的速度。

根据美国银行全球研究报告，到 2030 年，AMD 的每股盈利能力可能超过 30 美元，大约是该行今年预期 7.62 美元的四倍。 这个差距就是整个论文。

美国银行告诉投资者在未来 90 天内停止对 AMD 进行评级，并开始在本世纪末对一家与今天完全不同的业务进行定价。

该银行 620 美元的价格目标是基于 2028 年盈利预期的 27 倍，与 AMD 自己的五年历史交易区间一致。

投资者仍在对未来 90 天进行评级

市场尚未跟上这一框架。 据 CNBC 报道，AMD 第二季度营收创纪录，达到 115 亿美元，调整后每股收益为 1.66 美元，均高于华尔街预期，但该股在下一个交易日下跌了 9%。

数据中心收入较上年同期增长了一倍多，但投资者关注的是利润指引持平以及与新人工智能基础设施相关的资本支出不断增加。

这种反应正是美国银行告诉客户要忽略的近期噪音。 该银行的报告认为，AMD 的旗舰机架级人工智能系统 Helios 直到第四季度才会对业绩产生有意义的影响，因此根据本季度的利润线来判断股票完全没有抓住重点。

AMD现在卖的是机架，而不仅仅是芯片

Helios 代表了 AMD 实际销售产品的转变。 AMD 现在不再像几十年来那样运输单独的处理器和图形芯片，而是将 GPU、CPU 和网络硬件封装到完整的机架系统中，Nvidia 多年来一直使用这种格式来销售整个 AI 计算机而不是松散的组件。

AMD 已经与愿意大规模押注这一转变的客户签约。 Meta 承诺在一份多年协议中提供高达 6 吉瓦的 AMD GPU 容量，OpenAI 也达成了类似的 6 吉瓦协议，微软和甲骨文今年也准备部署 Helios 系统。
